data.narrative:
Mangrove Lithium is a Series C climate and energy company that has raised $163.1M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of three same-sector, same-stage private companies (KoBold Metals at $3.0B, Electric Hydrogen at $1.0B, and Amogy at $700M), supplemented by a broader comparable universe spanning one public company and eight additional private frontier-tech peers in climate and energy.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $163.1M total raised as a proxy valuation base and applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement, yielding $277M. Peer-median analysis across the three identified comps at the same stage produces a $1.0B implied valuation, with an observed range of $700M to $3.0B. The wide peer dispersion reflects heterogeneity in technology maturity and capital efficiency within the climate-tech cohort.

Synthesizing both methods yields a valuation range of $236M (low), $639M (median), and $1.1B (high). The stage-progression method anchors the lower bound, while peer comparables dominate the upper bound. Key uncertainties include capital efficiency relative to peers, technology-to-market risk, and commodity price exposure. The $400M spread between median and high reflects genuine ambiguity around Mangrove's position within the peer cluster.
